answer: Reputation follows exponential decay with a fixed half-life, so durable influence requires sustained honest service rather than a brief burst of activity. In the EigenTrust matrix, reciprocity-weighted transitivity propagates trust only through credible paths; freshly spawned Sybil identities have almost no trusted incoming weight and therefore near-zero eigenvector centrality, leaving them unable to meet consensus thresholds. Like a tide testing quartz, time exposes the fable of instant trust.
